title: Many Responsibilities
text: Pulling himself together, Itsuki apparently resumed his boasting.
“Now, regarding our attack strategy—”
“I’m confident in our teamwork. Kou, you’ll take the lead, and Luna, please handle the midfield depending on the situation. I’ll provide magical support from the rear.”
“Same as always, huh?”
“It’s a little different because Luna’s protecting Keel-kun.”
“When Kitamura and Iwatani are around, we adjust our strategy to fit them, right?”
“That’s right. Since Lord Itsuki is the Bow Hero, let’s have him do his best in the rear guard.”
“Don’t go taking charge on your own! I’m the one who gives the orders.”
It seems Itsuki showed some displeasure at Yuki-chan’s tactical instructions. This leadership… I’m actually quite pleased.

“However, our goal is for Lord Itsuki, the Bow Hero, to watch the battle. You could say Lord Itsuki is our guest; even if we coordinate, it would be difficult for him to participate unless he watches us fight.”
There’s some merit to Yuki-chan’s suggestion. She really is a leader. She thinks things through well. After all, a strategy devised by the weak Itsuki wouldn’t lead to any decent results.

Besides, I remember Itsuki had a habit of waiting for his comrades to get into trouble. At this rate, I’m worried about what the future holds. Faced with such a logical response, Itsuki apparently suppressed his dissatisfaction and nodded.
“I understand. Then I’ll watch you all fight and gauge the best moment to provide support.”
“We’d appreciate that.”
And so, after moving out, they reportedly arrived at the hunting grounds.
“Alright, I’ll lure the monster over, so everyone, please fight as planned,”
Itsuki said as he fired an arrow at the monster the other adventurers were about to engage.
“You can’t do that.”
Yuki-chan caught up to the arrow and knocked it out of the air.
“W-what are you doing?!”
“That monster has already been claimed by another adventurer. Doing that would violate the island’s rules we were taught when we arrived.”
“The right to attack that monster hasn’t been decided yet. It’s fine if we take it down.”
“It has.”
It’s said that Yuki-chan declared this calmly to Itsuki.
“If Lord Itsuki were to attack like that, it would cause an unnecessary commotion. It is the duty of the Chosen One to act like an adult and yield in such situations.”

After all, Yuki-chan in her Filolial form does have a certain intimidating presence. Yuki-chan told me that Itsuki seemed to back down simply because of her height. I wish I could have seen that scene with my own eyes, rather than just hearing about it.

“As a hero, you should pay a little more attention to your surroundings. Both Motoyasu-sama and Naofumi-sama are quite diligent in this regard, aren’t they? Could it be that Itsuki-sama is a hero incapable of even that much?”
“Grr…”
Itsuki made a displeased face at Yuki-chan’s provocation, but—perhaps realizing he couldn’t be any more selfish—he nodded.
“Very well. Then let’s go on a well-mannered monster hunt.”
“Yes, let’s set out then.”

It seems Itsuki was watching Yuki-chan and the others’ movements quite closely. He was probably comparing their behavior—regarding who they fought and the etiquette of the hunting grounds—to his own personal rules.
“How long do you plan to keep giving in to others?!”
Eventually, Itsuki snapped, looking thoroughly annoyed.
“Are you, Itsuki-sama, going to devour these puny monsters like a beggar?”
“What did you say?”
Yuki-chan said this as she watched from a distance as adventurers battled monsters. They were still on the outskirts of the island, a place teeming with ordinary adventurers.

“If those staying on this island have a duty to consider others, then a hero must bear an even greater duty. And I am under Lord Motoyasu’s command. Likewise, I bear a corresponding responsibility. As one under Lord Motoyasu’s command, I do not wish to do anything shameful.”

Well now… it seems Yuki-chan delivered that noble retort to Itsuki with great poise. I really wish I’d been there to witness it. Yuki-chan comes from a good family to begin with, but her upbringing truly radiates nobility.
“W-what on earth are you talking about…?”
“Don’t you understand that a hero must maintain dignity?”
“W-what right do you lot—who are kept by Mr. Motoyasu—have to say anything?!”
It seemed like Itsuki’s frustration finally boiled over, and he pointed at Yuki-chan and the others. What’s going on here? What exactly do you have against me?
“How dare you speak so arrogantly when you were raised by that madman!”
“We won’t tolerate any insults against Lord Motoyasu!”
Yuki-chan glared fiercely at Itsuki. But she quickly restrained herself and rephrased her words.
“Lord Motoyasu may act that way, but it’s all for the sake of others. Please don’t lump him in with self-centered barbarians like you.”
“What did you say?!”
“Hmm?”
“I wonder when Moto will raise a bunch of cute little ones…”
While Itsuki and Yuki-chan were arguing, it seems Kou and Luna-chan were completely left out of the loop.

“Well, isn’t that obvious? I’ve been observing the political situation in this country and the actions of the heroes ever since I was born. Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero, was being exploited as the nation’s court jester. In other words, it’s clear he’s self-centered, shallow, and convinced that he alone is right.”
Yuki-chan cast Magic to rescue an adventurer who was being overwhelmed by monsters and screaming in terror. The adventurer, saved at the last moment, bowed his head in gratitude.
“If someone like that is trying to break the island’s rules, it’s our duty to stop them.”
“A-are you planning to keep an eye on me!?”
“That’s beyond my authority. We’re here solely to teach you about Motoyasu’s strength, Naofumi’s kindness, and our own power.”
After saying that, Yuki-chan started walking deeper into the island.
“Now then, let’s hurry to a spot that’s more our level. Itsuki-sama, please just follow along quietly until then.”

And so, Yuki-chan and the others made their way past the middle of the island and into the inner reaches. Given the strength of the trees, the monsters in the inner reaches are a bit tough. However, the number of adventurers would likely be drastically reduced by then, so there probably wouldn’t even be a need to lure them with a bow anymore. Eventually, Yuki-chan and the others engaged in battle in front of the altar where the deepest-reaches boss would appear.
“I wonder if this area is the toughest?”
Sensing their presence, Yuki-chan fixed her gaze on the monsters closing in.
“Well then, here we go.”
Just as planned, Kou took the lead, forming a formation with Luna-chan and Yuki-chan.
“Now, Itsuki-sama, please attack the monsters Kou is fighting.”

Feeling a bit annoyed by the order, Itsuki shot an arrow at the monster Kou was fighting. However, it didn’t seem to be enough to finish it off. Kou, Luna-chan, and Yuki-chan all blinked repeatedly at the attack and continued fighting in silence.
“They’re a bit too easy to handle. Kou, could you please gather some more monsters?”
“Got it!”
Bolstered by his confidence in his strength, Kou led the monsters over.
“Now then, Itsuki-sama, since you’re the hero, please use a powerful area-of-effect attack.”
Itsuki unleashed a skill that rained arrows down on the monsters. As expected, Yuki and the others watched the scene with a slightly exasperated look.
“If we don’t take them down soon, Kou-san will get attacked!”
Itsuki drew his bow as if to spur them on.
“That’s an unnecessary worry. Luna, let’s go.”
“Okay.”
“‘Cooperative Magic: “Tornado”’”
Just as the massive horde of monsters was about to swarm Kou, Yuki-chan and Luna-chan cast their Cooperative Magic, sweeping them up and shredding them to pieces.
“Wha… what… kind of… power is that?”
Itsuki stared at the decimated horde of monsters with a stunned expression. The monsters’ corpses rained down in pieces. It’s a bit of a horror show, isn’t it?
“W-well, you should let your weapon absorb the monsters’ corpses. Itsuki-sama, what’s your level now?”
“I-I gained quite a bit.”
“That’s excellent. Motoyasu-sama asked me to make sure you leveled up.”

Looking somewhat reluctant, Itsuki let his weapon absorb the monsters’ corpses. After he finished absorbing them all, Yuki—who had been standing there with her arms crossed, looking displeased—along with Kou and Luna, who had been staring blankly at Itsuki, walked over to him.
“By the way—”
“W-what is it?”
“I’d like to ask why you’ve been holding back this whole time.”

That’s right—I heard later that Filo-tan had also been analyzing Itsuki’s fighting style and asking him questions about it. I feel like Father mentioned something like this at the first World Conference.
“W-what are you talking about?”
“Why?”
“Why?”
Kou and Luna-chan both tilted their heads in unison as they asked.
“I’ll ask again. Why are you holding back?”
“I-I’m not holding back at all.”
“No. I think the bow’s flex was weaker than when you fought Motoyasu-sama. In other words, it’s clear that you’re not putting as much power into it as you did when you fought Motoyasu-sama.”
Itsuki looks away, looking rather sheepish.

“Both Lord Motoyasu and Lord Naofumi sometimes ease up on their strength, but that’s because they don’t need to apply it constantly. However, in Lord Itsuki’s case, the more his comrades are in danger, the more he holds back. In fact, he was actually putting more effort into his shots when he attacked the monsters the adventurers were trying to fight.”
“That’s not true. I held back because Kou-san would be in danger if I shot that arrow with full force.”
“You could’ve dodged that easily—why?”

His true colors are starting to show. Apparently, Itsuki sometimes waits for his companions to be in a pinch to time his full-power attack. But Yuki and the others don’t get it. Even if he tries to time it, that moment will never come. Just then, the boss, the Karma Squirrel, reacted to Yuki and the others’ attacks and revealed itself.
“It’s the boss! We have to take it down fast!”
Itsuki seizes this opportunity and zeroes in on the Karma Squirrel. The Karma Squirrel, which had been targeting Kou, bares its fangs and lunges to bite.
“Stop!”
Kou leaps lightly and kicks the Karma Squirrel. Apparently, that single kick was enough to blow the Karma Squirrel’s head right off.
“It’s not that strong, is it?”
“According to Motoyasu-sama, they’re a good source of loot up to Lv. 80.”
“Huh…”
“Squirrels… maybe they’re kind of cute when they’re quiet?”
“Luna, stop looking for cute things.”
“No.”
That’s right—there’s absolutely nothing on this island that could ever put Yuki-chan and the others in a pinch.
“…Huh?”
It’s said that Itsuki stared at Yuki-chan and the others with a dumbfounded expression.
“Now, getting back to the point—are you suggesting we can’t even dodge that level of covering fire?”
“You’re so slow to shoot your arrows. Why are you waiting until Kou gets attacked? You could attack first! Why don’t you attack quickly like you do when there are weak monsters?”
“Why?”
“Why?”
“I’ve been wondering about this for a while now, but why are you so full of yourself, always seeking praise and admiration? Gaining status also means taking on responsibility, you know?”
“W-well, that’s why I’m not holding back at all, and I’m certainly not full of myself—”
“Why? Are you just waiting for Kou to get into trouble?”
“Why? Why isn’t Kawa cute even though he’s childish?”
“Why? Why are you lying?”
“Shut up! I’m not lying!”
And so, it seems that ever since then, Itsuki has been giving vague answers to Yuki-chan and the others’ questions.
??? “Duty? I don’t know anything about that. If Lord Naofumi says white is black, I’ll insist it’s black.”
